proposal.hypothesis: For rows with 33–64 elements, grouping eight warp-aligned rows into each 256-thread CTA should reduce CTA count versus the prior four-row mapping while retaining contiguous lane access within each row. This may trade off against occupancy or latency hiding. The two prior valid T1 programs measured 34.147 ms and 34.678 ms for the full call; neither isolates the effect of these kernels. This experiment tests CTA group size rather than asserting a speedup.

retained: For L <= 32, pack floor(256/L) rows per CTA using a two-dimensional block, preserving one output thread per element.
For 33 <= L <= 64, assign one 32-lane warp to each of eight rows in a 256-thread CTA; each lane processes positions at a stride of 32.
For L > 64, retain one-row 256-wide output tiles.
Keep forward and input-gradient kernels separate, preserve bounds-safe padding and FP32 arithmetic, and leave the weight-gradient computation unchanged.
